advisory.finding: The submit error handler catches (URLError, OSError, ValueError), but http.client.HTTPException subclasses, notably IncompleteRead raised by resp.read() on a truncated body, inherit only from Exception. These still escape as a traceback with exit 1 and never reach reconciliation, even though the commit says an unreadable response is now reconciled. The same gap exists in _add_hashtag and in _reconcile's own re-read.
scenarios: A proxy cuts off the submit response mid-body after Gerrit has merged. IncompleteRead propagates, the script crashes with exit 1, and the merge is misreported.
The hashtag POST hits a truncated response. The exception escapes _add_hashtag and blocks the submit, contradicting 'a failure only warns'.
advisory.suggested_fix: import http.client and use a shared tuple such as `_TRANSPORT_ERRORS = (urllib.error.URLError, http.client.HTTPException, OSError, ValueError)` in all three except clauses.

advisory.finding: The fake _request in _post_vote_failure gives the same `reread` dict to every GET after the first, whatever the path. No test can tell whether the reconcile re-read actually asks for ?o=ALL_REVISIONS. If _read_all_revisions were swapped for the existing read_change (o=CURRENT_REVISION), every test would still pass. Yet the Rebase-If-Necessary case this code exists for would then exit 1 on a real Gerrit, because only the rebased current revision would come back.
merged_from: The non-HTTP branch of the new _add_hashtag, `except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, ValueError)`, has no test. The only hashtag test injects an HTTPError, which the earlier `except urllib.error.HTTPError` arm catches, so a timeout or connection error on the hashtag POST is never exercised.

No test raises a bare OSError (for example TimeoutError or ConnectionResetError) from the submit request. The timeout test wraps the timeout in URLError, which only matches how urlopen reports a timeout while connecting. A timeout during `resp.read()` is raised as a bare TimeoutError, and that case reaches the new `OSError` member of the except tuple, which no test covers.
scenarios: A refactor reuses read_change for the reconcile re-read. Tests stay green, but a change merged via a rebased patch set (submitted SHA no longer current) is reported as failed with exit 1.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the merged-path tests, keep `calls` and assert `any(m == "GET" and "o=ALL_REVISIONS" in p for m, p in calls)`. Or have fake_request drop `_SHA` from `revisions` when `"ALL_REVISIONS" not in path`, so the rebase case fails if the wrong read is used.

The test test_merged_check_requires_the_submitted_revision only covers the case where the SHA is absent. No test covers a MERGED change whose current_revision is a newer patch set that is not a rebase of the submitted one.
dropped.finding: _reconcile treats the submit as successful (exit 0, 'submitted: ... merged (revision X)') whenever the change is MERGED and the submitted SHA appears anywhere in ALL_REVISIONS. ALL_REVISIONS always lists every older patch set. So if another session uploaded and merged a newer, reworked patch set while this submit failed with a 5xx or timeout, the script reports success for content the operator never inspected. That defeats the script's revision-scoped purpose.
scenarios: The submit POST times out. Meanwhile another session pushes PS N+1 with different code and submits it. The re-read shows MERGED with both SHAs, and this script prints 'submitted ... merged (revision <old>)' and exits 0.
dropped.suggested_fix: Accept as merged only if detail['current_revision'] == revision, or every patch set after `revision` has RevisionInfo.kind in {'TRIVIAL_REBASE','NO_CODE_CHANGE','NO_CHANGE','MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE'}. Otherwise report that the change was merged at a different revision and exit non-zero. Add a test where the newer merged patch set has kind REWORK.

dropped.finding: The rewritten exit-code help says exit 1 means 'a re-read shows the change is not merged at the revision'. The code also exits 1 when the re-read itself fails, and then nobody knows whether the change merged. A caller who trusts the help may take exit 1 to mean 'definitely not merged' and resubmit or re-push a change that already landed.
scenarios: The submit POST times out after Gerrit has merged, and the follow-up GET also fails. The script exits 1, and the help says exit 1 means the change is not merged.
